start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:find-unexplored-ground with count 10, near small bakeries, keeping the rows in list unexplored-ground."

lists.label: Unexplored ground
lists.holds: One little-explored area, how well it fits the person, why and the evidence it is unexplored.

values.area: How early shift times change a small bakery team's health
values.because: Matches the person's skill in running a bakery and their aim to look after their body.
values.evidence: A search of trade and health papers found two surveys on bakers and none on shift times in small shops.

values.area: Why people leave short queues at small food stalls
values.because: Matches what they keep returning to: the Saturday bread queue.
values.evidence: Searches found studies of long queues at large shops, none of short queues at stalls.
values.answer: This pulls at me because I count walk-aways every Saturday.

instructions: 1. Pour the example rows into the list where you keep research ideas (see pour), or let the keep step make list:unexplored-ground.
2. Say "Run workflow:find-unexplored-ground" with count (10 to 1000, 100 when left out), near and list_id if you want them.

3. The AI works person, areas, match, ask and keep: it reads who you are first, finds little-explored areas with the search that shows how little exists, ranks each by fit, asks you about the best few one question at a time and keeps every area as a row.
4. Read the rows ranked by fit; answer the open questions in your own words.

worked_examples.title: Reading the person comes before searching for ground
worked_examples.ask: Find unexplored ground near small bakeries.
worked_examples.given: The pursuit pursuit:example-bakery says the person runs a one-shop bakery and wants more time for their body; the About me list says they teach new bakers; their messages return to the Saturday bread queue. Read from the person step of the workflow row.
worked_examples.hands_back: The submit shape of step person: {"skills":["bread baking","teaching new bakers"],"aims":["run a bakery that leaves time for their body"],"values":["plain honest food"],"draws_them":["the Saturday bread queue"],"sources":["pursuit:example-bakery","About me list","messages from the last month"]}

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
